questions.question: If 8A5146B is divisible by 88, then what is the value of B-A? यदि 8A5146B, 88 से विभाज्य है, तो B-A का मान क्या है?
questions.solution:
A number is divisible by 88 when it is divisible by both 8 and 11.

8A5146B is divisible by 8 only if its last three digits i.e., 46B is divisible by 8.

So, B = 4

Now, 8A51464 is divisible by 11 only if the difference of the sum of its digits at odd places and sum of its digits at even places is either 0 or a number divisible by 11.

Difference = (8 + 5 + 4 + 4) - (A + 1 + 6) = 14 - A

So, A = 3

Therefore, B - A = 4 - 3 = 1

We know, (a + b + c)2 = a2 + b2 + c2 + 2ab + 2bc + 2ac

62 = 32 + 2(ab + bc + ac)

ab + bc + ac = 2

Now, a3 + b3 + c3 - 3abc = (a + b + c)(a2 + b2 + c2 - ab - bc - ac)

189 - 3abc = 6(32 - 2)

189 - 3abc = 180

3abc = 9

abc = 3

Therefore, abc - 3 = 3 - 3 = 0

Let the cost prices of articles A and B are ₹ 4a and ₹ 5a respectively.

Selling price of A = 110% of 4a = ₹ 4.4a

Selling price of B = 120% of 5a = ₹ 6a

Now, 6a - 4.4a = 480

1.6a = 480

a = 300

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. He opened the door for his mother.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

He opened the door for his mother.

options.text: The door was opened by him for his mother.
options.html: The door was opened by him for his mother.

options.text: The door was open by him for his mother.
options.html: The door was open by him for his mother.

options.text: The door had been opened by him for his mother.
options.html: The door had been opened by him for his mother.

options.text: The door is opened by him for his mother.
options.html: The door is opened by him for his mother.

questions.solution:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of verb is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

The Active voice in this question is in Past Indefinite. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in Past Indefinite.

The format of Active voice is: Subject + V2 + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + was/were + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

For example:

Real Madrid won the Champions League. (Active Voice)

The Champions League was won by Real Madrid. (Passive Voice)

The options except (a) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (a): The door was opened by him for his mother.

questions.question: Sentences of a paragraph are given in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. The interest rates offered depend on the bank, deposit amount and the tenure you choose. B. It not only helps you to save money but also helps you to earn a substantial interest on it. C. One of the best ways to secure your money is by investing in fixed deposits. D. Under the fixed deposit scheme, the depositor deposits the money only once at the time of opening the account.
questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. The interest rates offered depend on the bank, deposit amount and the tenure you choose.

B. It not only helps you to save money but also helps you to earn a substantial interest on it.

C. One of the best ways to secure your money is by investing in fixed deposits.

D. Under the fixed deposit scheme, the depositor deposits the money only once at the time of opening the account.
questions.solution:
Sentence C comes first as it introduces the topic of the passage - 'fixed deposits'.

Sentence D follows and explains the fixed deposit scheme and sentence B explains its benefit (earning a substantial interest). Sentence A explains that thisinterest earned depends on the bank, deposit amount and tenure.

So, the correct order is CDBA.

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. This is /too grave sin / to be / pardoned.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

This is /too grave sin / to be / pardoned.
questions.solution:
In formal writing, the structure 'too + adjective + a + noun + infinitive' is used.

Some examples: This is too good an opportunity to lose.

Sheena is too good a speaker of English to make a mistake like that.

This is too cheap a mobile to be able to run that game.

So, there is an error in the part mentioned in option (b).

The correct sentence is: This is too grave a sin to be pardoned.

Hence, option (b) is the answer.

questions.solution:
The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the "to be" verb and the preposition 'by' is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

The Passive voice in this question is in Present Continuous tense. Thus, the Active voice will also be in Present Continuous.

In Passive voice, the format is: Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + am/is/are + being + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case).

Thus, the format of Active voice is: Subject + am/is/are + V1 + ing + Object.

For example:

A document is being typed by Arnab. (Passive Voice)

Arnab is typing a document. (Active Voice)

The options except (b) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Active Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (b): They are translating the poems of great English poets into other languages.

questions.question: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain a grammatical error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'no error' as your answer. Antique diamond necklace / was stolen / from the museum.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain a grammatical error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'no error' as your answer.

Antique diamond necklace / was stolen / from the museum.
questions.solution:
There is an error in part in option (c).

An article (either 'an' or 'the') should precede the phrase 'antique diamond necklace' to denote the identity of the diamond necklace to the reader. Depending upon whether it's known or unknown to the reader, 'a' or 'the' would precede the phrase.

So, the correct sentence is: An/the antique diamond necklace was stolen from the museum.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'. The investigation revealed that both of they had given false information to obtain the certificates.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.

The investigation revealed that both of they had given false information to obtain the certificates.
questions.solution:
When we use both as part of a subject or object which is a pronoun, it may be followed by of + an objective pronoun.

So, the subjective pronoun 'they' should be replaced with the objective pronoun 'them'.

Option (d) rectifies this error.

Option (b) is incorrect as the singular noun 'investigation' is followed by the plural verb 'reveal'.

The correct sentence is: The investigation revealed that both of them had given false information to obtain the certificates.

Hence, option (d) is the answer.

Note: Subjective Pronouns: The pronouns I, you, we, he, she, it, and they are known as subjective pronouns because they act as the subjects of verbs: We went to the party.

Objective Pronouns: The pronouns me, you, us, him, her, it, and them are called objective pronouns because they act as the objects of verbs and prepositions: Anjali drove us home.

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech. She said, "it is too good to be true".
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

She said, "it is too good to be true".

options.text: She said it were too good to be true.
options.html: She said it were too good to be true.

options.text: She said that it was too good to be true.
options.html: She said that it was too good to be true.

options.text: She is saying that it is too good to be true.
options.html: She is saying that it is too good to be true.

options.text: She says that it is too good to be true.
options.html: She says that it is too good to be true.

questions.solution:
The sentence in the Direct Speech is in Simple Present Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Indirect Speech should be in Simple Past Tense.

Simple Present (Subject + V1 + Object) should be converted into Simple Past (Subject +V2 + Object).

"That" is used in place of Inverted Commas while transforming the sentence from Direct Speech to Indirect Speech.

For example:

He said, "I never go to the village." (Direct Speech)

He said that he never went to the village. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

'Said' will be changed to 'said that'.

'Is' will be changed to 'was'.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (b): She said that it was too good to be true.

questions.solution:
The blank should be filled with the adjective starting with the vowel sound (as it follows the indefinite article 'an') to qualify the noun 'age'.

So, 'young' cannot fill in the blank.

Also, 'ignorant' and 'infant' are not appropriate adjectives for 'age'.

So, 'early' is appropriate to fill in the blank.

Note: Definite and indefinite articles: In the English language, we have one definite article 'the'; it refers to or introduces, a particular, specific noun. 'An' and 'a' are indefinite articles; they refer to, or introduce, an unspecified noun.
